description: Aztec Noir — high-level DSL for writing ZK circuits (Rust-like syntax, compiles to ACIR for Barretenberg backend). Supports UltraHonk (fast, modern), Groth16 (compact, on-chain), Plonk. Best DX of the Rust-family ZK frameworks for small-to-medium circuits. Use when prompt names Noir / Aztec / nargo / Barretenberg, or when you want high-level-DSL productivity over raw primitives.

buildHints.whenToUse: Attach for products with small-to-medium ZK circuits where the DSL's ergonomics beat writing raw R1CS. Excellent for verifier-side browser/Node proving — bundle stays manageable because Barretenberg wasm is <5MB. For huge circuits where performance dominates, reach for SP1/RISC Zero instead.
firstSteps: In circuits/: `nargo check` validates, `nargo compile` produces target/circuit.json (ACIR)
JS side: `import { Noir } from '@noir-lang/noir_js'; const noir = new Noir(circuit); await noir.execute(inputs)`
gotchas: Noir version pinning matters — the @noir-lang/noir_js version must match the nargo compiler you compiled with. Mismatches produce cryptic 'unknown opcode' errors.
Browser Barretenberg ships as WASM — first-load cost is ~3-5MB. Lazy-load behind a user-triggered action, not on page-mount.
Field arithmetic is mod BN254; large u64/u128 values need to stay under ~2^254.
